5 August 2026

Economic Bulletin Issue 3/2026

Foreword

This issue of the Economic Bulletin presents the ECB's assessment of the euro area economy and of monetary policy.

Economic activity

Economic activity is expected to continue to expand at a moderate pace over the coming quarters.

Real GDP is estimated to have expanded by 0.4% in the first quarter of 2026.

Real GDP growth is projected to increase from 1.2% in 2026 to 1.4% in 2027.

Domestic demand is expected to be the main driver of growth over the projection horizon.

Prices and costs

Headline inflation is projected to average 2.4% in 2025, 2.0% in 2026 and 1.9% in 2027.

Core inflation is projected to average 2.3% in June 2026.

Inflation expectations remained well anchored.

Financial developments

Bank lending rates are estimated to have reached 4.2% in June 2026.

Financing conditions remained tight, and monetary policy transmission continued to function smoothly.

Fiscal developments

Fiscal policy is expected to remain neutral over the projection horizon.

Monetary policy developments

The Governing Council decided to keep its key interest rates unchanged.

The Council stood ready to adjust all of its instruments within its mandate.

Risk assessment

Risks to economic growth were broadly balanced.

Upside risks to inflation remained, mainly reflecting energy and food prices.

Legal notice

This document is provided for information purposes only. It does not constitute a commitment by the European Central Bank.
